c.tagline: Golden mosques rise beside a river of stilted water villages.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are relatively scarce and often need to be booked by phone rather than hailed on the street; metered but a surcharge applies at night (9PM-6AM).

avoid.reason: Very safe; Sharia law — no alcohol, dress modestly

hood_desc: The historic downtown core along the Brunei River, with the golden-domed Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque, Tamu Kianggeh market and the Yayasan complex; walkable, central, and best for first-time visitors who want sights and river views on foot.

Stilted traditional houses over the Brunei River reachable by water taxi; staying in a homestay here suits travelers wanting an authentic cultural immersion, though amenities are basic and it's a short boat ride from downtown.
Brunei's modern commercial hub packed with malls, the famous night market and countless restaurants; suits travelers who want dining, shopping and nightlife-lite convenience over historic charm.

A leafy, slightly upscale residential and business enclave between downtown and Gadong with expat cafes and quieter streets; good middle-ground base for business travelers and those wanting a calmer stay near amenities.

A coastal stretch north of the city near Jerudong Park and Muara Beach, anchored by the luxury Empire Hotel & Country Club; suits travelers seeking a resort/beach escape and golf, willing to trade walkability for scenery and a 25-30 minute drive to downtown.

water.note: Generally treated to standard, but avoid it if discolored (common after heavy rain); bottled water is a safe extra precaution.

sys.n: Purple Line City Bus (Land Transport Dept. licensed vans)
Express buses to Kuala Belait, Seria, Tutong

transit.pay: Fares on the purple city buses are paid in cash directly to the driver/conductor (flat B$1 within the city, B$2 from the airport); exact change is appreciated. Water taxis (perahu tambang) to Kampong Ayer are hailed from riverside jetties and paid in cash per crossing, typically B$1-2. There is no rechargeable transit card system.
transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6:30AM-6PM at 20-30 minute intervals on most routes; there is minimal to no late-night public transport, so taxis or ride-hailing apps are needed after dark.
transit.note: The bus network is limited and infrequent by regional standards; most visitors rely on taxis, hotel transfers, or rental cars to get around efficiently.

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected in Brunei; a service charge (usually 10%) is already added at most hotels and mid-to-upscale restaurants, and rounding up for good service is appreciated but optional.

food.name: Ambuyat
food.desc: Brunei's national dish: glue-like sago starch twirled on bamboo chandas and dipped in sour cacah sauce, eaten with a spread of side dishes.

places.name: Aminah Arif Restaurant
places.note: The best-known ambuyat house in Brunei; full set with cacah and side dishes.

places.name: Salera Babu Restoran
places.note: Local favourite for ambuyat sets at everyday Bruneian prices.

places.name: Gadong mall food courts
places.note: Quick, cheap ambuyat plates when the specialist restaurants are full.

food.name: Nasi Katok
food.desc: Brunei's unofficial national snack - a parcel of hot rice, fried chicken and sambal wrapped in paper, sold around the clock for pocket change.

places.name: Kiulap nasi katok counters
places.note: Row of stalls widely rated the city's best; try the ayam penyet version.

places.name: Gadong Night Market
places.note: Evening market where dozens of stalls sell nasi katok and grilled snacks.

places.name: Tamu Kianggeh
places.note: Central open-air market with cheap cooked-food stalls from early morning.

food.name: Satay
food.desc: Skewers of chicken, beef or lamb marinated in turmeric and lemongrass, charcoal-grilled and dipped in thick peanut sauce with rice cakes.

places.name: Gadong Night Market
places.note: Rows of charcoal grills; the smokiest satay in the capital after dark.

places.name: Tamu Kianggeh
places.note: Riverside market grills serving satay and grilled fish through the day.

places.name: Aminah Arif Restaurant
places.note: Grilled meats and traditional sides served alongside its ambuyat sets.

food.name: Udang Sambal Serai Bersantan
food.desc: Royal Bruneian dish of prawns simmered in lemongrass, chilli and coconut milk; rich, fragrant and a standard partner for ambuyat.

places.name: Aminah Arif Restaurant
places.note: Served as part of the traditional ambuyat spread with cacah and greens.

places.name: Salera Babu Restoran
places.note: Home-style Bruneian cooking, strong on coconut-milk seafood dishes.

places.name: Gadong mall food courts
places.note: Malay stalls plate it up with rice for a fast, affordable lunch.

food.name: Kuih Melayu
food.desc: Bruneian sweets - crunchy kuih cincin, deep-fried penyaram, kelupis rice parcels and pandan-scented steamed cakes, sold by the bag.

places.name: Tamu Kianggeh
places.note: Morning market is the classic place to buy homemade kuih and kelupis.

places.name: Gadong Night Market
places.note: Wide spread of sweet and savoury kuih from early evening onwards.

places.name: Gadong mall food courts
places.note: Bakery counters and stalls selling kuih alongside coffee all day.

food.name: Soto and Mee Sapi
food.desc: Clear spiced beef or chicken broth over rice cakes and noodles, topped with fried shallots; Brunei's go-to breakfast and late-night bowl.

places.name: Tamu Kianggeh
places.note: Market stalls ladling soto from dawn, a local breakfast institution.

places.name: Kiulap shophouses
places.note: Cluster of casual eateries doing beef noodles and soto all day.

places.name: Gadong mall food courts
places.note: Reliable soto and noodle counters with air conditioning.

food.name: Teh Tarik
food.desc: Strong tea and condensed milk pulled between two jugs until frothy; the default drink at every Bruneian kopitiam. Brunei sells no alcohol.

places.name: Kiulap kopitiam
places.note: Coffee shops pulling teh tarik and kopi from breakfast until late.

places.name: Gadong Night Market
places.note: Drink stalls beside the grills, pulled to order in front of you.

places.name: Aminah Arif Restaurant
places.note: Teh tarik and local juices to finish an ambuyat meal.

food.name: Air Batu Campur (ABC)
food.desc: Mountain of shaved ice over red beans, jelly, sweetcorn and attap seeds, drenched in rose syrup, palm sugar and evaporated milk.

places.name: Gadong Night Market
places.note: Several ABC and cendol carts, the best cure for the equatorial heat.

places.name: Tamu Kianggeh
places.note: Market drink stalls making ABC and fresh fruit juices to order.

places.name: Gadong mall food courts
places.note: Dessert counters serving ABC and cendol in air-conditioned comfort.

landmarks: Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddin Mosque
This gleaming golden-domed mosque rises beside an artificial lagoon in the city center and is widely considered Brunei's most photographed religious landmark.
Kampong Ayer (Water Village)
Often called the Venice of the East, this sprawling stilt settlement on the Brunei River houses tens of thousands of residents in traditional wooden houses connected by boardwalks.
Jame'Asr Hassanil Bolkiah Mosque
With 29 golden domes and striking Mughal-inspired architecture, this vast mosque built to honor the Sultan's silver jubilee is one of Southeast Asia's most opulent places of worship.
Istana Nurul Iman
The world's largest residential palace and official home of the Sultan of Brunei, this immense gilded complex opens its doors to the public only during Hari Raya celebrations.
Royal Regalia Museum
This museum showcases the lavish ceremonial chariots, crowns, and coronation regalia of Brunei's monarchy, offering an intimate glimpse into the sultanate's royal traditions.
Brunei Museum
Perched on a hill overlooking the Brunei River, this national museum traces the sultanate's oil wealth, natural history, and Islamic art through extensive galleries.
Bandar Seri Begawan Waterfront
This scenic riverside promenade offers postcard views across the water to Kampong Ayer and the mosque domes, especially magical at sunset.
Tasek Lama Recreational Park
A lush rainforest park with a hillside reservoir and waterfall trails, offering visitors an easy escape into jungle greenery just minutes from the city center.
Malay Technology Museum
This riverside museum recreates traditional Bruneian crafts, boat-building, and stilt-house construction techniques that shaped Kampong Ayer's centuries-old way of life.
Proboscis Monkey River Safari (Brunei River)
A twilight boat cruise along the Brunei River offers a rare chance to spot the long-nosed proboscis monkeys endemic to Borneo swinging through riverside mangroves.

train.note: Brunei has no public railway (only a short disused private oil-company line at Seria). All overland travel is by road or ferry.

bus.note: International buses leave from central Bandar Seri Begawan and cross several immigration posts, so allow extra time. These Malaysian operators have no reliable official booking website - buy tickets at their BSB counters. Passport required.

intl.to: Labuan (Malaysia) - departs Serasa Ferry Terminal, Muara

ferry.note: Fast ferries to the Malaysian island of Labuan leave from Serasa Ferry Terminal at Muara, about 25 km from the city; from Labuan you can connect onward by ferry to Kota Kinabalu. Tickets are sold at the terminal. Carry your passport.
